name: Duqm
title: Duqm Drydock Thickness Measurement | Pre-Docking UTM
description: Thickness measurement at Duqm for ships docking at Asyad Drydock: pre-docking UTM to size steel renewal, in-dock hull gauging and renewal survey support.
h1: Pre-Docking and In-Dock Thickness Measurement for Ships at Duqm
intro: Most ships come to Duqm to dock. Asyad Drydock, formerly Oman Drydock Company, repairs and drydocks ocean-going tonnage on Oman's Arabian Sea coast, beside a commercial port that also serves the Duqm refinery. A superintendent bringing a ship here needs measured wastage before the yard can plan steel work, and often more gauging once the ship is in dock. We mobilise a team from India to Duqm and fit the readings to the docking timeline, from the anchorage through to undocking.

highlights.h: Steel estimates before the ship arrives
highlights.p: Gauging done before docking, at an earlier port or at the Duqm anchorage, gives the yard a measured steel list, so plate, sections and labour can be ready when the ship enters dock instead of being ordered after it.

highlights.h: In-dock access to the whole hull
highlights.p: Once the ship is in dock, bottom plating, bilge strakes, sea chests, rudder and stern areas become reachable. We gauge them alongside the yard's own work and re-measure renewed areas where the owner wants a record.

The southwest monsoon brings heavy swell to the Arabian Sea coast in summer, which makes launch transfers and anchorage gauging harder. We plan boat-dependent work for the calmer months and keep monsoon-season scope inside the yard.

port.h: Duqm: Drydock, Port and Special Economic Zone
p: Duqm was a small fishing town on Oman's central Arabian Sea coast before the state developed a special economic zone around it. Today the zone holds Asyad Drydock, the Port of Duqm with its commercial and liquid bulk terminals, a fishing harbour, and the Duqm refinery run by OQ8, a joint venture of OQ and Kuwait Petroleum International. The location sits close to the main shipping lanes between the Gulf, the Red Sea and Asia, and outside the Strait of Hormuz, which is much of its appeal to owners choosing where to dock.

Ships stay long at Duqm because most are there for repair. A typical docking runs from arrival at anchorage, through entry into dock, to sea trials and redelivery, and gauging fits several points along that path: before entry, to confirm the steel estimate; in dock, for the bottom and the areas only reachable there; and after steel renewal, where the owner wants a record. Product tankers loading at the refinery jetties and cargo ships at the commercial berths make shorter calls, and ships booked for docking sometimes wait at anchorage for a dock to come free, which is itself a useful gauging window.

The inspection work here is shaped by what docking exposes. A tanker or bulk carrier arriving for its renewal survey brings a full gauging requirement, and an owner who has not gauged in advance discovers the size of the steel job only after the ship is in dock, when every day spent waiting for plate is a day off hire. Ships that have traded for years in Gulf heat and warm Indian Ocean water arrive with ballast tanks, sea-water lines and scrubber discharge piping in poor condition, and those are the areas where renewal most often outgrows the original specification. Measuring them early is the simplest way to keep a docking on its planned length.

facilities.h: Where Gauging Is Done at Duqm
p: Asyad Drydock is the centre of gauging work at Duqm. Its dry docks give full access to the underwater hull and, once tanks are gas-freed and ventilated, to cargo, ballast and fuel tanks without the time pressure of a cargo call. The yard's afloat repair berths, used before or after docking, suit tank and deck gauging that does not need the ship out of the water. We work within the yard's permit-to-work system and coordinate with the yard's production team and the class surveyor's attendance, so that readings are ready when the surveyor walks each space.

Outside the yard, the Port of Duqm's commercial and liquid berths handle cargo ships and product tankers loading at the refinery, and the anchorage holds ships waiting for docking or a berth. Pre-docking gauging at anchorage is practical in calm weather, but launch transfers become difficult in the southwest monsoon, so anything that depends on boats should be done earlier in the voyage or deferred until the ship is alongside. Duqm is remote, so our technicians travel with their own gauges, probes, couplant and calibration blocks rather than relying on local supply.
list: Asyad Drydock, dry docks — bottom plating, bilge strakes, sea chests, rudder, stern frame and tank gauging during the docking period
Asyad Drydock, repair berths — afloat gauging of cargo, ballast and fuel tanks, decks and piping before or after the ship enters dock
Duqm anchorage — pre-docking gauging to confirm the steel estimate while the ship waits for its dock, weather permitting
Port of Duqm liquid berths — deck, piping and accessible tank gauging on product tankers loading refinery cargo
Port of Duqm commercial berths — hold and deck gauging on bulk, general cargo and container ships during their call
Earlier ports on the voyage — gauging at Sohar, Salalah or a Gulf port before the ship sails for Duqm, when the steel list is needed early

context.h: Regulation and Owner Context for Ships Docking at Duqm
p: Oman applies port state control under the Riyadh MoU, though for a ship in dock the more immediate authority is class: the renewal survey defines the gauging extent, and the attending surveyor decides where additional readings are needed when substantial corrosion turns up. For ESP ships, meaning oil tankers, bulk carriers and chemical tankers, the third renewal survey and later ones bring extensive gauging of cargo and ballast tank structure, and that is the docking where preparation pays off most. The Arabian Sea is outside any emission control area, so the 0.50% global sulphur cap applies, and docking is the usual time for scrubber maintenance and the overboard piping inspection that goes with it.

The ships that dock at Duqm come from a wide catchment: Gulf, Red Sea and Indian Ocean trades, with owners and managers in the Gulf states, India and further afield. For them, Duqm is one option alongside yards in the UAE, Bahrain and elsewhere, and the choice often turns on dock availability and the ship's route. Gauging ahead of arrival lets an owner compare yards on the same measured scope, and gives the technical superintendent a firm basis for the docking budget and off-hire planning. For hull gauging at Duqm, that preparation is what turns a yard estimate into a work list.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Duqm
jobs.p: Thickness measurement at Duqm is tied to the docking calendar. The most useful jobs happen before the ship enters dock, because they turn an estimated repair specification into a measured one; the in-dock work then covers what can only be reached with the ship out of the water, plus any areas the surveyor adds. Where an owner wants a renewal record, we return to the renewed areas before undocking.
list: A bulk carrier arriving for its third renewal survey: holds, hopper tanks and topside tanks gauged at anchorage so the yard can prepare steel before the ship enters dock
A crude tanker in dock: bottom plating, bilge strakes and sea chests gauged in dock, with cargo tank deckheads and bottom longitudinals measured as tanks are gas-freed
A container ship docking for scrubber repairs: wash-water discharge and overboard piping gauged on the repair berth before the ship enters dock, to define the pipe renewal
A product tanker loading at the Duqm refinery jetties: ballast tank and deck piping gauging to prepare for a CAP assessment requested by a charterer
A second-hand purchase docking at Duqm before entering service with its new owner: condition gauging of hull, tanks and piping for the new owner's records

logistics: The usual route is through Muscat International Airport, then a domestic flight to Duqm Airport or the long drive south through Al Wusta. Asyad Drydock and the Port of Duqm control access through their own security; the yard or the ship's agent arranges passes for each technician and their equipment, and launches for anchorage work. Indian technicians travel on Omani business visas, applied for as soon as the docking date is fixed. Because dockings are booked well ahead, the visa lead time rarely constrains the job, and we confirm accommodation in Duqm at the same time.

faqs.q: When should pre-docking gauging be done for a ship booked into Asyad Drydock?
faqs.a: Early enough for the yard to act on it. Gauging at a convenient earlier port, where tanks can be emptied and made safe, gives the yard time to prepare steel and the owner time to compare the result with the repair specification. Gauging at the Duqm anchorage just before entry still helps, but it leaves less room to adjust the plan or the docking length.

faqs.q: Can you gauge the bottom and sea chests while the ship is in dock at Duqm?
faqs.a: Yes, those areas are the reason in-dock gauging matters. Once the hull is cleaned and the yard's staging or access equipment is in place, we gauge bottom plating, bilge strakes, sea chests and gratings, the rudder and stern areas, and any shell plating the surveyor marks. Coordinating with the yard's blasting and painting sequence is important, so that readings are taken before coating work closes the area.

faqs.q: Does the southwest monsoon affect thickness measurement at Duqm?
faqs.a: It affects the anchorage more than the dock. During the summer monsoon, swell along the Arabian Sea coast makes launch transfers and work on ships at anchor difficult, sometimes impossible. Work inside the dry dock or on the repair berth carries on, so in those months we move anchorage scope into the yard period or to an earlier port.

faqs.q: Can you gauge our ship at another port first and then meet it at Duqm?
faqs.a: Yes. A common pattern is to gauge cargo and ballast tanks at a loading or discharge port where the ship is empty and accessible, such as Sohar, Salalah or a Gulf port, then send the team to Duqm for the in-dock part. The two sets of readings go into one report, so the yard and the surveyor see a single picture of the ship.
